findings.reason: the section should extend `reckon/budget.py:2934 recorded_windows` (adding a per-session breakdown beside its per-backend one) and name it, rather than re-deriving a lagging ledger-only figure, which is the same "a forked state reader drifts from its owner" defect the rubric names.
findings.text: §4's done-when requires "what they are shipping" per session drawing the window, and the plan sources that from the ledger ("the ledger records what each run spent") while `recorded_windows()` already reads each live session's window draw by its rollout receipt and session id, fenced through `reckon/crew/rollout.py`; the plan names neither `budget.py` nor `directory.py` (the "who" owner chosen by the `shared-window-source` decision) as the mechanism to extend, so the node will build a parallel per-session aggregation that drifts from the fresher rollout-sourced reading the pre-flight already paces to

findings.reason: the section must either state that the advisory is added to the run event the follower renders (extending `ticker.py`) or justify why the follower cannot read it, because the committed `done-when` as worded is already satisfied by §3's row carry and would let the node close without ever touching the channel the `advisory-delivery-point` decision actually locked (dispatch-and-follower).
findings.text: §8's whole deliverable is a follower line ("the advisory arrives where the choice is made"), but the section names no mechanism and gives no reason the follower's existing lane cell cannot carry it; `reckon/crew/ticker.py:_lane_cells` already renders the lane mean from the lane document (`lane.json`) and never reads the per-dispatch `lane_advisory`, so the advisory does not ride any watch-stream field the follower sees

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the advisory is a single carry dict behind the dispatch payload, and §6 reuses `reckon.capabilities`' own routing helpers (`_routing_outcome_exclusion`, `_write_paths`, `_charged_cost`, `_median_or_none`) rather than wrapping them, so the plan does not spread complexity across shallow wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §4 re-derives per-session window draw from the ledger, duplicating the per-session window reader already owned by `reckon/budget.py` and the coordinator enumeration owned by `reckon/crew/directory.py`.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1470, cli, mcp and refusal families unchanged by any open section; §7 states the binding constraint ("adds no new command and no new tool") and the landed §2/§3 nodes honoured it by riding existing calls, and no open section proposes a new CLI option, MCP view or refusal family.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan cites the mechanisms it extends (the gate's advisory mode, the `requested_backend` precedent at `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:3411`, the coordinator directory and ledgers chosen by the `shared-window-source` decision, and the ledger's routing figures for §6); the one reused surface it fails to name is captured under duplicate_owner.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §8 adds a follower line carrying the advisory without saying why the existing lane cell in `reckon/crew/ticker.py` cannot be extended to carry it.
